text:
Avery: Thanks team — quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Can someone clarify the difference between our 'regional buffer pools' and 'burst buckets'? I heard EMEA is getting a separate prewarm path — what's the expected lead time and SLA impact?

Sam: Short answer — buffer pools are very short-lived warm slots (think <5m warm window) used to shave tail latency for interactive requests. Burst buckets are longer reserved capacity we can bring up for sustained load (>30m).

Priya: Where do we see which customers are mapped to burst buckets vs served on-demand? CS needs that mapping for support comms.

Diego: There's a new capacity dashboard under infra -> Capacity -> Buffer vs Burst (added last week). https://console.redwood/internal/boards/capacity :eyes: It shows mapping by customer tag and current headroom per region.

Marta: A couple of clarifications from ops/leadership: 1) EMEA prewarm (separate buffer pool) is on the Q2 runway but depends on GPU procurement timing and validation. 2) If procurement lags, default fallback is automatic routing to quantized model variants + reduced batch sizes to maintain SLOs.

Avery: Thanks — can someone post a short runbook snippet for that fallback flow so PMs/CS can explain user impact?

Marta: Posted a quick snippet below, will expand into a full runbook in Confluence by EOD Tue:

```# simplified fallback runbook
if capacity.low:
  route -> quantized-variant (preserve latency SLOs)
  scale_policy -> reduce_batch_size
  notify -> #support + oncall
  enable_retries -> 2x with jitter
```

Sam: Action items from this thread: Marta to publish full runbook by EOD Tue, Diego to pin the capacity dashboard to the all-hands notes and share the direct link, Priya to export a customer mapping for reserved buckets by tomorrow, and I'll schedule a 15m sync with Product and CS to align messaging. :calendar:

InfraBot: Runbook page created: https://confluence.redwood/infracapacity/fallback-runbook :white_check_mark:

Avery: Awesome, thanks everyone — will loop back after the sync. :thumbsup:
